judgments.justification: “highest structural adherence” with highest Match Scores and lowest Levenshtein distances under both automatic and human evaluation matches the finding.
It gives selected content comparisons but omits the vanilla ROUGE-L comparison, Claude FactCC exception, and marginal AlignScore lead.
“indicating that the beam variant is the more effective configuration” compares edit with beam, whereas F3 requires the mixed comparison with vanilla LLaMa-3-8B.
Fine-tuned LLaMa is mentioned only as structurally below beam; its comparison with vanilla, including ROUGE-L and FactCC, is not reported.
It reports the single run and absent tests but omits variance estimates and the human evaluation’s 100-summary, two-annotator scope.
It does not discuss reuse of the guiding classifier, best-of-16 selection, or the resulting potential circularity.
“highest automatic Match Score,” “lowest automatic Levenshtein,” and corresponding highest/lowest human metrics correctly establish beam’s strongest structural adherence.
“did not show a consistent content-accuracy cost” is supported by the correct ROUGE-L, Claude FactCC exception, and near-leading AlignScore comparisons.
“lower structural adherence than the beam variant” uses beam as the comparator and therefore does not report the required edit-versus-vanilla mixed result.
It correctly covers structural metrics and reduced ROUGE-L but omits the fine-tuned model’s increased FactCC, an essential mixed component.
No single-run, variance, significance-testing, or human-evaluation-scope limitations are reported.
Classifier reuse, best-of-16 selection, circularity, and the independence and scope of human evaluation are not discussed.
“numerically highest structural adherence” and the reported automatic and human Match Score and Levenshtein values correctly cover all structural metrics.
It compares content only with DeepSeek and vanilla LLaMa, omitting Claude’s higher FactCC and the system-wide AlignScore characterization.
“indicating that the beam variant is the more effective configuration” substitutes a beam comparison for the required edit-versus-vanilla comparison.
The effects of fine-tuning relative to vanilla LLaMa on structural metrics, ROUGE-L, and FactCC are not reported.
“No statistical tests,” “single-run,” and “100 summaries per model and two annotators” correctly support descriptive-only interpretation and human-evaluation scope.
Although human evaluation is scoped, the passage does not identify classifier reuse, best-of-16 selection, or potential circularity.
